description_preview:
Superhuman offers a dynamic hybrid working model for this role. This flexible approach gives team members the best of both worlds: plenty of focus time alongside in-person collaboration that fosters trust, innovation, and a strong team culture. This role requires at least 2 days per week in our San Francisco or Seattle hub.
About Superhuman
Grammarly is now part of
Superhuman
, the AI productivity platform on a mission to unlock the superhuman potential in everyone. The Superhuman suite of apps and agents brings AI wherever people work, integrating with over 1 million applications and websites. The company’s products include Grammarly’s writing assistance, Coda’s collaborative workspaces, Mail’s inbox management, and Go, the proactive AI assistant that understands context and delivers help automatically. Founded in 2009, Superhuman empowers over
40 million people, 50,000 organizations, and 3,000 educational institutions
worldwide to eliminate busywork and focus on what matters. Learn more at superhuman.com.
The Opportunity
We’re hiring
early-career Software Engineers
who want to learn fast, ship real product, and build AI-native software used by millions.
From day one, you’ll work on production systems- not toy problems- alongside experienced engineers who care deeply about craft, judgment, and impact. You’ll contribute to features across our core products, learn how large-scale systems are designed and shipped, and develop a strong engineering foundation in a modern, AI-first environment.
This is a role for engineers who are curious, thoughtful, and excited to turn ideas into real outcomes.
What You’ll Do
As a Software Engineer At Superhuman, You Will
Ship production-grade code that impacts over 40 million daily active users across our suite of AI-powered productivity tools
Build and iterate on features for Grammarly, Coda, Superhuman Mail, and Go
Work with cutting-edge AI technologies and modern web frameworks
Collaborate closely with product, design, and engineering teams to deliver delightful user experiences
Develop AI-native features that leverage large language models, natural language processing, and intelligent automation
Learn how to build large-scale distributed systems that are highly available and reliable
Learn best practices around system design, testing, deployment, and scalability
Contribute to technical discussions and help shape the direction of your team’s projects
Grow rapidly through mentorship, feedback, and hands-on ownership of real projects
Make a meaningful impact on the lives of millions of people who rely on our products every day
What We’re Looking For
Must-haves
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience), graduating in 2026 or 2027
Strong foundation in computer science fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, and software design
Proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g., Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, Go, C++)
Experience building software through internships, personal projects, open source contributions, hackathons, or coursework
AI native and experienced in using AI coding agents like Claude code, cursor, and Codex for productivity gains
Solid understanding of system design, databases, and back-end architecture
Excellent communication skills and ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams
A demonstrated ability to work independently with minimal guidance, proactively manage tasks and priorities, analyze and execute work efficiently, and thrive in a fast-paced, results-driven environment
Nice-to-haves
Previous internship experience at a technology company
Experience with web tech (React, Node.js, TypeScript)
Exposure to AI/ML tools, APIs, or frameworks (e.g., OpenAI, LangChain, TensorFlow, PyTorch)
Familiarity with modern engineering workflows (Git, CI/CD, testing frameworks)
Track record of shipping projects end-to-end
Comfort navigating ambiguity and learning new technologies quickly
Compensation And Benefits
Superhuman offers all team members competitive pay along with a benefits package encompassing the following and more:
Excellent health care (including a wide range of medical, dental, vision, mental health, and fertility benefits)
Disability and life insurance options
401(k) and RRSP matching
Paid parental leave
20 days of paid time off per year, 12 days of paid holidays per year, two floating holidays per year, and flexible sick time
Generous stipends (including those for caregiving, pet care, wellness, your home office, and more)
Annual professional development budget and opportunities
Superhuman takes a market-based approach to compensation, so base pay may vary by location. Our US locations are categorized into two compensation zones based on proximity to our hub locations.
Base pay may vary considerably depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The expected salary ranges for this position are outlined by compensation zone and may be modified in the future.
For more information about our compensation zones and locations where we currently support employment, please refer to this page. If a location of interest is not listed, please speak with a recruiter for additional information.
Why You’ll Love It Here
Learn by doing:
You’ll work on meaningful problems with real users, not shadow projects
Strong mentorship:
Learn from engineers who’ve built and scaled products at companies like Google, Facebook, and Dropbox
Real ownership:
We trust early-career engineers with responsibility and support them as they grow
Connected culture:
Highly collaborative teams, in-person connection, and shared wins

About The Team
The Release Management team owns the infrastructure and process that gets validated software out the door — release cuts, version uprevs, build pipelines, and artifact management — across our automotive platform. We collaborate with Program Validation for release gate sign-off and work alongside the Embedded, UX/HMI, and OTA domain teams to maintain release momentum and prevent last-minute emergencies.
About The Role
We are looking for a Build & Release Engineer to own release cuts from our Git repositories, manage uprevs (dependency/firmware version updates), build and maintain our CI/CD pipelines, and administer build artifact management. You will also own our internal Release Management portal — the system where all build artifacts and binaries are tracked, managed, and released — as its primary engineer. This hands-on software engineering position demands robust coding proficiency alongside deep CI/CD expertise, as you will actively build and maintain a live application rather than just configuring pipelines.
At Applied Intuition, You Will
Release Engineering & Orchestration
Execute release cuts from Git repositories across multiple product lines and branches.
Manage version uprevs end to end, coordinating dependency and firmware bumps with upstream teams.
Define and own release branching, tagging, and versioning strategies.
Investigate and resolve complex build failures, coordinating fixes across development teams.
CI/CD Infrastructure
Design, build, and maintain scalable software release CI/CD pipelines for build, test orchestration, and deployment.
Automate build infrastructure to reduce manual effort and enforce pipeline quality gates.
Troubleshoot pipeline failures to ensure high availability and reliability for development teams.
Artifact Lifecycle Management
Own the artifact lifecycle, including versioning, signing, storage, and cross-environment promotion.
Maintain strict artifact provenance and traceability from commit to release.
Administer and optimize artifact repositories (e.g., Artifactory).
Internal Tooling & Portals
Develop and maintain the internal Release Management portal — the system of record for build artifacts, binaries, and release status.
Ship new features for the portal as its primary engineer, including UI, backend services, and external integrations.
Integrate the portal with CI/CD systems, artifact repositories, and downstream release workflows.
Cross-Functional Alignment
Partner with the Program Validation team and TPMs on release gate criteria and final sign-off.
Coordinate with domain teams (Embedded, UX/HMI, OTA etc) on release timing, risks, and blockers.
Communicate release status and critical path risks to stakeholders.
We're Looking For Someone Who Has
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field and graduating by December 2026 or Summer 2027.
3+ years of professional software development experience, with strong coding ability in at least one modern language (e.g., Python, Go, Java, or JavaScript/TypeScript)
Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines (e.g., Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Buildkite)
Strong Git experience, including branching, tagging, and release workflows
Experience with artifact management systems (e.g., JFrog Artifactory, Nexus, or equivalent)
Experience designing, building, or maintaining internal tools or portals
Strong troubleshooting skills across build, dependency, and release issues
Nice To Have
Front-end development experience (e.g., React, TypeScript) for extending internal tooling UIs
Experience with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes)
Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP)
Experience with embedded/automotive release processes (multi-ECU uprevs, ASPICE-aligned release workflows)
Experience with monitoring/observability tools (Grafana, Kibana, Splunk)
Experience with Jira, Polarion, or similar issue tracking tools

The BAE Systems GXP Software Team is seeking highly motivated engineering students to join our team as an intern. We are looking for candidates that will enjoy developing unique, cutting-edge solutions that help people make sense of exquisite imagery, video, and other sophisticated remote sensor data. We value those who are curious to explore the "what", "when", "how", and "why" of world events using advanced technologies. We encourage attitudes towards problem solving driven by persistence, innovation, teamwork and a willingness to meet challenges head on.
Our team develops state-of-the art software for sensor-data processing, analysis, storage, and visualization for challenging problems in the areas of video analytics, image processing, and other temporal data sources. We utilize the most advanced techniques for data science, machine learning, computer vision, statistical analysis, and cloud computing to discover hidden patterns in big data. We develop end-to-end applications that process data for desktop, web, embedded platforms, and large scale cloud computing environments. We believe collaboration is key, as such, you will be paired with a mentor to facilitate a smooth onboarding process as you become familiar with our products and the technologies we employ.
Our flexible work environment provides you a chance to change the world without giving up your personal life. We put our customers first – exemplified by our mission: “We Protect Those Who Protect Us®.” Sound like a team you want to be a part of? Come build your career with BAE Systems.
Our Commercial Software Products Include
GXP InMotion Server - ingests and streams real-time data feeds, providing recording and analytics capabilities
GXP InMotion Desktop - video and image analysis application
Track Analytics Software Suite (TASS) - a suite of algorithms for analyzing geospatial data
MOVINT Database - a geospatial big-data store with RESTful web service interfaces
GXP InMotion Web / MOVINT- a browser-based front end for visualizing and analyzing geospatial data
You can read more about our software and solutions here:
InMotion Desktop and Server - https://www.geospatialexploitationproducts.com/content/gxpinmotion/
MOVINT Solutions - https://www.geospatialexploitationproducts.com/content/movint/
Responsibilities
As an intern, you will be working directly embedded with one of our small software teams. Depending on your background and interests your responsibilities may include one of the following:
Implementing new features in our web-based, cloud, and server-based products.
Investigating new technologies and open-source software into our products.
Designing new enhancements to our software.
Working with a mentor to learn about software principles / technical development.
Development in Python, C++, Java, and/or JavaScript.
In this position, you will participate in BAE Systems' nationwide LEAP Internship & Co-op Program, where you will Learn, Engage, Apply, and Progress within the company. The LEAP Program will provide you with the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals on impactful projects, engage in career development opportunities, and network with our business leaders and the other students in the program.
Because this role involves a combination of collaborative/in-person and independent work, it will take the form of a full-time on-site work format.
Required Education, Experience, & Skills
Enrolled in an accredited engineering/technical undergraduate or graduate degree program pursing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics
Basic understanding of and skills in software design and coding, including object-oriented analysis & design.
Exposure to at least one of Python, C++, Java, or JavaScript.
Know how to profile, optimize, and test your own code
Motivated to develop skills in new technical areas, solve challenging and unique problems, and enjoy working on a range of assignments.
Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills
While not critical to the open position, experience with the following skills are useful in our organization and will be helpful as you expand your roles and responsibilities:
Course work one or more: Algorithms, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Architecture, Computer Graphics, Computer Networking, Data Science, Database Systems, Machine Learning, Operating Systems, UI/UX Design, Cloud technologies
Familiarity with software development/engineering, including requirements analysis, software development, installation, integration, evaluation, enhancement, maintenance, testing, and problem diagnosis/resolution.
Experience with IDEs such as Visual Studio, PyCharm, or NetBeans.
Experience with configuration management tools such as git.
Experience with build systems such as cmake, Maven, or Ant.
Experience with one or more of image processing, data science, or machine learning.
Pay Information
Full-Time Salary Range: $46437 - $62721
Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.
Temporary employees generally are not eligible for BAE Systems benefits, but can elect to participate in the 401(k) savings plan. Temporary employees working 20+ hours per week are eligible for medical benefits, the employee assistance program, and business travel accident insurance.

BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. description_preview:
Technology & Engineering Junior Full-Time, Senior Individual Contributor
About The Role
The Platform Engineer is responsible for the technical infrastructure that makes ACPWB's analytical work possible. The Technology & Engineering team of 19 builds and maintains the employee data warehouse that powers our advisory practice, and this role is central to ensuring that infrastructure is reliable, secure, and scalable. Our analytical staff depends on this work. So do our clients, indirectly. You will know both are counting on you.
The Platform Engineer will join ACPWB's Technology & Engineering team to drive internal systems performance and security improvements to the employee data warehouse. Working in Terraform and AWS, you will partner with data engineers, analysts, and business stakeholders to build solutions that have measurable impact on firm performance. We deploy frequently, review code carefully, and invest in the quality of our technical foundation.
Key Responsibilities
◆ Participate in sprint planning, standups, and retrospectives as part of the Technology & Engineering engineering cadence
◆ Maintain network and systems infrastructure for ACPWB's Milwaukee office and remote work environments
◆ Ensure reliability, performance, and security of internal systems performance and security infrastructure on Amazon Web Services (AWS)
◆ Design, build, and maintain components of the employee data warehouse using Terraform and AWS
◆ Contribute to ACPWB's technical roadmap by identifying investment opportunities in internal systems performance and security
Qualifications
Required
◆ 1+ years of experience managing or contributing to production systems with reliability requirements
◆ Demonstrated ability to write clean, tested, maintainable code with attention to documentation
◆ Strong troubleshooting and debugging skills with the ability to diagnose issues under time pressure
◆ Experience with version control (Git), code review practices, and CI/CD pipelines
Preferred
◆ Experience with Python for data processing including pandas, NumPy, or PySpark
◆ Prior experience in a professional services or advisory firm technology environment
◆ Experience with data orchestration tools such as Apache Airflow, Prefect, or equivalent
◆ Demonstrated interest in data quality, data contracts, or observability as engineering practices
WHY ACPWB
Our culture is one of intellectual honesty, high standards, and what we describe internally as 'aggressive collaboration' — a phrase that means we challenge each other's thinking constructively and support each other's success unconditionally. We have won awards for this. The awards are real. The culture is also real.
ACPWB was founded in Milwaukee in 2006 with a simple mandate: help working Americans understand and advocate for the compensation they deserve. Eighteen years later, that mandate has grown into a full-service research and advisory practice serving clients from early-stage employers to Fortune 50 enterprises — and we are still based in Milwaukee, because Milwaukee is genuinely underrated.
INTERVIEW PROCESS
Candidates will complete a two-stage process: a 45-minute exploratory call followed by a comprehensive final interview including a skills demonstration. We do not require unpaid work samples. We do require genuine expertise. These are different things.
What Success Looks Like In Year One
◆ Document the components of the employee data warehouse you own at a level sufficient for another engineer to maintain them
◆ Lead at least one sprint or project phase end-to-end from planning through deployment
◆ Ship at least two meaningful features or improvements to the employee data warehouse with full documentation
◆ Develop a thorough working knowledge of the employee data warehouse architecture, data flows, and dependencies
Ready to Apply?
Applications for this position are being accepted through November 9, 2026. Submit your materials using the form below.
Apply for This Position →

description_preview:
WHAT MAKES US A GREAT PLACE TO WORK
We are proud to be consistently recognized as one of the world’s best places to work. We are currently the top ranked consulting firm on Glassdoor’s Best Places to Work list and have earned the #1 overall spot a record seven times.
Extraordinary teams are at the heart of our business strategy, but these don’t happen by chance. They require intentional focus on bringing together a broad set of backgrounds, cultures, experiences, perspectives, and skills in a supportive and inclusive work environment. We hire people with exceptional talent and create an environment in which every individual can thrive professionally and personally.
WHO YOU’LL WORK WITH
As the premier consulting partner for the private equity industry, Bain's PEG boasts a global practice that is over three times larger than any competitor. Our network of over 1,000 professionals supports private equity and institutional investor clients through every stage of the investment life cycle, from deal generation and due diligence to portfolio value creation and exit planning.
Bain & Company is developing a suite of cutting-edge data and software solutions designed to revolutionize how the private equity industry uses data for investment insights and decision-making.
The PEG Innovation team's mission is to create analytical solutions for Bain clients, teams, and the broader institutional investor space using proprietary software and data products. This includes the development, commercialization, and daily management of Bain's proprietary datasets, data, and software businesses.
WHERE YOU’LL FIT WITHIN THE TEAM
Platform Engineers build and maintain the shared backend services that power the Bain Diligence Platform (BDP). These include enterprise SSO, session management, audit, case and case-provenance APIs, document and file access (Microsoft Graph / SharePoint and Azure Blob Storage), search with source citations, and the API gateway. You contribute to services across the full delivery lifecycle — design, build, test, deploy, monitor, and operate — with guidance from senior engineers. You write reliable, well-tested code, follow platform engineering standards, and help ensure services are secure-by-default, observable, and production-ready. You collaborate closely with Platform, Data & Intelligence, Security, and Infrastructure teammates to deliver shared capabilities that are stable, scalable, and easy for squads to consume as the platform hardens.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Core Platform Service Development, Deployment, and Operations (80%)
Implement backend features and service endpoints in existing platform services under the guidance of senior engineers.
Build and maintain REST APIs in FastAPI using clear contracts, input validation, and consistent error handling.
Write and update Postgres schemas and Alembic migrations using safe patterns (including backwards-compatible changes) with review support.
Use Redis for standard platform patterns such as caching, session storage, and rate limiting under established conventions.
Use event-driven integration where asynchronous behaviour adds clear value (for example change feeds and domain events, following existing schema and envelope conventions), consistent with the platform's simple-now, evolve-when-needed approach.
Add and maintain service instrumentation: structured logs, OpenTelemetry-style spans, and Datadog metrics and APM traces according to platform standards.
Update and maintain Helm chart values and Kubernetes manifests for services deployed to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS); ensure probes, resource requests/limits, and environment configuration are correct, and support blue/green candidate/promote deployments.
Contribute to Terraform infrastructure-as-code for Azure, deployed through env0 / Terraform Cloud across dev, UAT, and prod environments, with review support.
Work within GitHub Actions pipelines: pull-request test suites, branch-to-environment promotion (main → Dev, release/X.Y → UAT/Prod), image publishing to Cloudsmith, and blue/green candidate/promote deploys with approval gates.
Triage and resolve routine production issues for owned services; participate in on-call rotation with support and follow established runbooks.
Write and update runbooks and service documentation for changes you ship, ensuring operational steps remain accurate.
Other (20%):
Participate in code reviews as both author and reviewer; incorporate feedback and apply engineering standards consistently.
Use AI coding assistants to accelerate boilerplate creation (routers, schemas, tests, docs); review all generated code and align it with platform conventions before committing.
Use LLMs to draft first-pass documentation (runbook updates, service notes, API docs); validate and refine outputs before publishing.
Collaborate with Security and Infrastructure on implementation tasks (e.g., Azure Key Vault secret consumption, Entra ID app registrations, network-security-group / private-endpoint constraints, least-privilege configuration, and Wiz security-scan findings) under guidance.
Contribute to quality improvements (test coverage, refactors, observability, and reliability fixes) as part of regular delivery work.
ABOUT YOU
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)
2+ years of experience building backend services, APIs, or platform components in a production or near-production environment.
Demonstrated experience building and maintaining backend services or APIs with an emphasis on reliability and correctness.
Experience contributing to REST APIs and working with relational databases (Postgres preferred), including basic schema evolution and migration workflows.
Exposure to containerised development and deployment practices (Docker) and familiarity with operating services in Kubernetes environments (Azure / AKS in practice).
Exposure to authentication and authorisation concepts (JWT, RBAC,

Surescripts serves the nation through simpler, trusted health intelligence sharing, in order to increase patient safety, lower costs and ensure quality care. Job Summary
The Data Governance Engineer is part of our Data Trust & Enablement team within the Enterprise Data Platform. This role is central to how we build confidence in our data - across the teams that produce it, the systems that move it, and the stakeholders who depend on it. This position supports the architecture and execution of our enterprise data quality framework, bringing engineering rigor and automation to problems that today rely too heavily on manual discovery and reactive fixes. This role works alongside data engineers, architects, platform engineers, analysts, and governance leads to make data trust a first-class property of how we build and operate our data platform. This is not a documentation-only or policy role. It is an engineering role on a team that believes governance should be automated, observable, and embedded in the development lifecycle.
Responsibilities
Help architect and build the foundational framework that defines what trusted data means at Surescripts across dimensions of completeness, accuracy, freshness, consistency, and fitness for purpose.
Translate abstract data quality concepts into concrete, measurable, automatable rules that can be applied at scale across the medallion architecture.
Develop and maintain data contracts between producing and consuming teams, with tooling that catches violations before they reach downstream systems.
Integrate governance checks into developer workflows so that quality and compliance are default behaviors, not afterthoughts.
Contribute to and extend our metadata platform (data catalog, lineage, tagging) to support discoverability, trust scoring, and impact analysis.
Help design and implement the automated pathway through which a data asset moves from unvalidated to certified, including rule execution, scoring, threshold management, and integration with Collibra for catalog-level certification status.
Make certification a first-class part of the data product delivery lifecycle.
Coach teams on trust and governance standards and help them instrument their pipelines.
Serve as a subject matter expert on governance best practices for data engineers, analysts, and product teams. Advocate for and implement a "trust by design" principle across the platform engineering and data product development workflows.
Help define the organization-wide vocabulary and standards for data trust: what a critical data element is, what certification means, what the difference is between a validated asset and a trusted one.
Partner with the Trust and Enablement leadership to ensure standards are enforced in Collibra and visible to business stakeholders.
Qualifications
Basic Requirements:
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, business administration, or related field
2+ years of experience in data engineering, data platform development, or a closely related field with a demonstrated focus on data reliability and observability.
Prior experience with Collibra data quality, Monte Carlo, Great Expectations, or equivalent.
Hands-on experience designing and implementing data validation frameworks, quality rule engines, or observability pipelines, ideally in a cloud-native environment.
Strong SQL skills and experience working with Big Query or a comparable cloud data warehouse at scale.
Experience integrating data trust or quality metadata into a data catalog-Collibra experience is a strong plus.
A platform engineering mindset - focus on systems, frameworks, and reusable patterns, not one-off fixes.
Ability to communicate trust concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders, including governance teams, product owners, and business leaders.
Preferred Qualifications

title: Software Engineer
reason: Stack +11; Title fit +12; US +10
description_preview:
About Foundation Health
Foundation Health is an AI operating system for pharmacy - built by a team who lived the problem firsthand, not one that came to healthcare from the outside. Every day, prior authorizations delay prescriptions, pharmacists lose hours to paperwork instead of patients, and prescriptions slip through the cracks between health systems. We believe thoughtfully applied AI can finally change that - deep, integrated infrastructure that streamlines how care is coordinated, purpose-built for the complexity of specialty pharmacy.
We're building toward a world where pharmacy teams spend their time on patients, not paperwork - where AI handles the routine so clinicians can focus on what only humans can do. Getting there takes the right people. We're looking for curious, ambitious folks who want to help solve healthcare's hardest problems - for our patients, our partners, and each other.
The Role
We've built an AI operating system for pharmacies, tackling the operational infrastructure behind things like paperwork and care coordination. It's in production with enterprise health systems across the US, and we're working directly with one of the biggest names in pharmacy.
As a Software Engineer, you'll ship features and fixes across the product: prior auth workflows, Epic integrations, and the AI agents that handle patient calls and texts. You'll own your work end to end, build with AI tools every day, and be trusted to make the call, from your first week.
At a big company, year one is usually internal tooling and six layers of review. Here, you'll ship to production in your first week, on systems pharmacists and patients actually depend on, in the same room as engineers who've built at serious scale.
What You'll Actually Do
Ship well-scoped features and fixes independently, with proper test coverage, at a pace you'll be proud of
Work AI-native from day one, with Claude, Cursor and the rest as a core part of how you build, and with the judgment to know when the output needs a second look
Learn the domain deeply: who the pharmacist is, what workflow they're stuck in, and why your ticket exists. Ask "why" when a requirement feels off
File the bugs and UX issues you notice without waiting to be told
Level up fast through code review and pairing with engineers who've built serious systems. Here, the feedback comes from customers, not committees
What We're Looking For
Sharp CS fundamentals and evidence you love building. That could be side projects, internships, open source, or a startup that didn't work: something you made because you couldn't not
Learning velocity. You pick things up fast and you enjoy the discomfort of not knowing yet
High agency, and curiosity about the product, not just the code
You're already building with AI tools and you think carefully about their limits
Where you'll work
This is a hybrid role, 3 days a week in our downtown Orlando office
, and early in your career that's a real advantage. Most of what makes a great engineer isn't written down anywhere. It's overhearing how a senior engineer argues a design through, or turning your chair round to ask a question instead of waiting a day for a Slack reply. Our VP of Engineering works from the same office. Everything is greenfield, so you'll learn on modern code, not by untangling someone else's ten-year-old mess.
The practical stuff
Our packages include equity, and it's early enough that it actually means something, not a rounding error. Orlando also means your comp survives contact with your cost of living, and Florida has no state income tax. We're backed by Define Ventures, led by a 2x founder, and our VP of Engineering came from DeepMind.

Job Title: Business Intelligence Reporting/ Web Developer
Locations
: Hybrid: Fort Worth, TX | Jacksonville, FL | New York, NY | Sacramento, CA

The BI Reporting & Web Developer is a hybrid technical role within the Unique Assets Development team, responsible for both enterprise reporting and client-facing web development. The developer will design and maintain SSRS reports and Power BI dashboards that surface trust accounting data to internal and external stakeholders, while also contributing to web-based applications and tools that support the team’s broader platform.
This role requires strong SQL skills, hands-on SSRS and Power BI experience, and proven web development capability. BI Report Development & Delivery

Web Development

Optimize query performance for large financial and trust accounting datasets

Collaborate with DBAs to ensure data quality, integrity, and access patterns are maintained

Partner with business analysts, QA, and operations staff through requirements gathering, UAT, and post-deployment validation
Engage stakeholders on adjacent legacy systems (e.g. Rocket Universe) to understand source data structure and lineage ahead of SQL replication
Document report logic, data sources, API contracts, and field definitions for maintainability
Support end-users with report and application questions, training, and ad hoc analysis
What You Will Bring:
3+ years of hands-on SSRS report development in a production environment
2+ years of Power BI development)
3+ years of SQL Server development with strong T-SQL proficiency
2+ years of web application development with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and at least one modern front-end framework (VueJS, React or Angular strongly preferred)
Experience working in financial services, trust accounting, wealth management, or another regulated industry preferred
Technical Skills
SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS) — paginated reports, subscriptions, RDL authoring, Report Builder

T-SQL — stored procedures, CTEs, window functions, query tuning and execution plan analysis

Source control — Git-based workflows, branching, pull requests
Data modeling fundamentals (star schema, normalization)

Experience with trust accounting or financial portfolio management platforms
Familiarity with data conversion and ETL processes
Familiarity with legacy database platforms such as Rocket Universe (UniData/UniVerse) for source data analysis
Experience with server-side web technologies (.NET, Node.js, or similar)
Understanding of TDD and automated testing practices in a regulated software environment

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Finance, or a related field; or equivalent professional experience

Analytical thinking — breaks down complex data problems and translates them into reliable, usable outputs
Technical versatility — able to shift effectively between reporting and web development work

Collaboration — works effectively across development, QA, BA, and operations teams

The National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NRAO), operated by Associated Universities, Inc. The team develops the real-time software that configures, controls, and monitors the Very Large Array (VLA), Very Long Baseline Array (VLBA), and Green Bank Telescope (GBT).
This role focuses on translating scientific observing requirements into the hardware configurations and commands required by antennas and digital signal processing systems. The position involves software development, domain modeling, troubleshooting, documentation, testing, and collaboration with scientists, engineers, and telescope operators. The work supports mission-critical software operating 24/7 at major scientific facilities and may contribute to the next-generation Very Large Array (ngVLA).

Design, implement, test, and maintain components of the online software used to configure and control the VLA, VLBA, and GBT in real time.

Model observing concepts including frequency setups, subband and baseband layouts, polarization products, timing, and integration structures.
Implement rules, constraints, and validation checks to determine which observing configurations are achievable on specific instruments.
Work from interface control documents and hardware specifications to ensure commands generated by the online system are correct and complete.
Diagnose and resolve issues across the layers between scientific observing specifications and telescope command streams.
Collaborate with telescope operators, engineers, scientists, and other technical staff to investigate and resolve system issues.

Participate in code reviews, testing, and release processes for mission-critical software.

Technical leadership experience with complex data acquisition, scheduling, and operational support systems.
